drivingQuestion: Where does one who erred in the Amida resume: from the blessing in which he erred, or from the start of that section?
outcomeNote: Rav Sheshet's refutation of Rav Huna is deflected by an אמר לך; the Rav Huna / Rav Asi dispute is left standing, and the rest of the unit is aggadic material on prayer length and naming.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָעוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה — צָרִיךְ לְסָרֵב. וְאִם אֵינוֹ מְסָרֵב — דּוֹמֶה לְתַבְשִׁיל שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מֶלַח. וְאִם מְסָרֵב יוֹתֵר מִדַּאי — דּוֹמֶה לְתַבְשִׁיל שֶׁהִקְדִּיחַתּוּ מֶלַח. כֵּיצַד הוּא עוֹשֶׂה: פַּעַם רִאשׁוֹנָה — יְסָרֵב, שְׁנִיָּה — מְהַבְהֵב, שְׁלִישִׁית — פּוֹשֵׁט אֶת רַגְלָיו וְיוֹרֵד.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The mishna teaches that one who replaces a communal prayer leader who erred in the middle of the Amida prayer should not refuse when approached. The Gemara cites the general halakha with regard to proper conduct when one is approached to serve as prayer leader. «The Sages taught» in a baraita: One who is approached «to pass before the ark» to serve as prayer leader, for the sake of propriety «should refuse,» to avoid creating the impression that he is too eager. «And if he does not refuse,» but jumps at the opportunity, «he is like cooked food without salt,» which is to say that he acts in bad taste. «However, if he refuses too much» this is similarly inappropriate, as «he is like cooked food that was ruined by» too much «salt.» So «how should he act?» The appropriate conduct when approached to serve as communal prayer leader is as follows: When approached «the first time, one should refuse; the second» time, one should «vacillate» like a wick that has just begun to catch a flame but is not yet burning; and «the third» time, «he should stretch his legs and descend» before the ark.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה רוּבָּן — קָשֶׁה, וּמִיעוּטָן — יָפֶה, וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: שְׂאוֹר, וּמֶלַח, וְסָרְבָנוּת.
segments.en: On this note, the Gemara cites that which «the Sages taught» in a baraita: There are «three» things that «are harmful in excess but are beneficial when used sparingly.» They are: «Leavening» in dough, «salt» in a cooked dish «and refusal» for the sake of propriety.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: טָעָה בְּשָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת — חוֹזֵר לָרֹאשׁ. בְּאֶמְצָעִיּוֹת — חוֹזֵר לְ״אַתָּה חוֹנֵן״. בְּאַחֲרוֹנוֹת — חוֹזֵר לָ״עֲבוֹדָה״.
segments.en: The mishna states that when one replaces the communal prayer leader, he commences from the beginning of the blessing in which the former had erred. However that is not universally true, as «Rav Huna said:» One who «erred in» any of «the first three» blessings «he must return to the beginning» of the Amida prayer because the first three blessing comprise a single entity. Likewise, if one «erred in» any of «the» thirteen «middle» blessings, «he returns to» the blessing of: «You grace» humanity, the first of the middle blessings. If one erred «in» any of the three «final» blessings, «he must return to the» blessing of «Temple service,» which is the first of the final blessings.

segments.he: וְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר: אֶמְצָעִיּוֹת אֵין לָהֶן סֵדֶר.
segments.en: «And Rav Asi» disputes one aspect of Rav Huna’s opinion, as «he said: The middle» blessings «have no» set «order.» If one erred in any of them he may insert it at whatever point he becomes aware of his error.

segments.he: מֵתִיב רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מֵהֵיכָן הוּא חוֹזֵר — מִתְּחִלַּת הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁטָּעָה זֶה. תְּיוּבְתָּא דְרַב הוּנָא.
segments.en: «Rav Sheshet raised an objection» based on a baraita: «From where does he» commence «repetition» of the Amida prayer? He commences «from the beginning of the blessing in which» the former «had erred.» If so, this is «a conclusive refutation of Rav Huna’s» opinion, as Rav Huna said that if one erred in one of the middle blessings, he returns to the beginning of the middle blessings, not to the beginning of that particular blessing.

segments.he: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא: אֶמְצָעִיּוֹת כּוּלְּהוּ חֲדָא בִּרְכְתָא נִינְהוּ.
segments.en: «Rav Huna» could have «said to you: The middle» blessings «are all» considered «one blessing;» commencing from the beginning of the blessing means returning to the beginning of the middle blessings.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לְעוֹלָם אַל יִשְׁאַל אָדָם צְרָכָיו לֹא בְּשָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת, וְלֹא בְּשָׁלֹשׁ אַחֲרוֹנוֹת, אֶלָּא בְּאֶמְצָעִיּוֹת. דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: רִאשׁוֹנוֹת — דּוֹמֶה לְעֶבֶד שֶׁמְּסַדֵּר שֶׁבַח לִפְנֵי רַבּוֹ. אֶמְצָעִיּוֹת — דּוֹמֶה לְעֶבֶד שֶׁמְבַקֵּשׁ פְּרָס מֵרַבּוֹ. אַחֲרוֹנוֹת — דּוֹמֶה לְעֶבֶד שֶׁקִּבֵּל פְּרָס מֵרַבּוֹ, וְנִפְטָר וְהוֹלֵךְ לוֹ.
segments.en: «Rav Yehuda said:» There is an additional distinction between the various sections of the Amida prayer: «One must never request his» own «needs in the first three or in the last three» blessings; «rather,» he should do so «in the middle» blessings. «As Rabbi Ḥanina said:» During the «first» three blessings, he «is like a servant who arranges praise before his master;» during the «middle» blessings, he «is like a servant who requests a reward from his master;» during the «final» three blessings, one «is like a servant who» already «received a reward from his master and is taking his leave and departing.»

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּתַלְמִיד אֶחָד שֶׁיָּרַד לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה בִּפְנֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְהָיָה מַאֲרִיךְ יוֹתֵר מִדַּאי. אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: כַּמָּה אָרְכָן הוּא זֶה! אָמַר לָהֶם: כְּלוּם מַאֲרִיךְ יוֹתֵר מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: ״אֵת אַרְבָּעִים הַיּוֹם וְאֶת אַרְבָּעִים הַלַּיְלָה וְגוֹ׳״?!
segments.en: Continuing on the subject of prayer, «the Sages taught:» There was «an incident where one student descended» to serve as prayer leader «before the ark in the presence of Rabbi Eliezer, and he was excessively prolonging his prayer. His students» complained and «said to him: How long-winded he is. He said to them: Is» this student «prolonging» his prayer any more «than Moses our teacher» did? «As about» Moses «it is written:» “And I prostrated myself before the Lord «for the forty days and forty nights» that I prostrated myself” (Deuteronomy 9:25). There is no limit to the duration of a prayer.

segments.he: שׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּתַלְמִיד אֶחָד שֶׁיָּרַד לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה בִּפְנֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְהָיָה מְקַצֵּר יוֹתֵר מִדַּאי. אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: כַּמָּה קַצְרָן הוּא זֶה! אָמַר לָהֶם: כְּלוּם מְקַצֵּר יוֹתֵר מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, דִּכְתִיב: ״אֵל נָא רְפָא נָא לָהּ״.
segments.en: There was «again an incident where one student descended» to serve as prayer leader «before the ark in the presence of Rabbi Eliezer, and he was excessively abbreviating his prayer. His students» protested «and said to him: How brief is his» prayer. «He said to them: Is he abbreviating» his prayer «any more than Moses our teacher» did? «As it is written» with regard to the prayer Moses recited imploring God to cure Miriam of her leprosy: “And Moses cried out to the Lord, saying: «‘Please, God, heal her, please’”» (Numbers 12:13). This student’s prayer was certainly no briefer than the few words recited by Moses.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: כׇּל הַמְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל חֲבֵירוֹ — אֵין צָרִיךְ לְהַזְכִּיר שְׁמוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֵל נָא רְפָא נָא לָהּ״, וְלָא קָמַדְכַּר שְׁמַהּ דְּמִרְיָם.
segments.en: Having mentioned Moses’ prayer for Miriam, the Gemara cites what «Rabbi Ya’akov said» that «Rav Ḥisda said: Anyone who requests mercy on» behalf of «another need not mention his name, as it is stated: “Please, God, heal her, please,” and he did not mention Miriam’s name.»

moves.summary: Baraita on the proper measure of refusing to lead prayer, brought against the mishna's 'should not refuse'.
moves.about: the etiquette of refusing when asked to lead prayer: refuse once, waver the second time, descend the third

moves.summary: Baraita: leaven, salt and refusal are harmful in excess and good in small measure.
moves.about: three things harmful in excess and beneficial in small measure: leaven, salt, refusal

moves.summary: Rav Huna: one who erred returns to the beginning of the section (first three, middle, or last three) in which he erred.
Rav Asi: the middle blessings have no fixed order.
moves.about: whether one who erred in a middle blessing must return to אתה חונן (Rav Huna) or may insert the blessing wherever he remembers, the middle blessings having no fixed order (Rav Asi)

moves.summary: Rav Sheshet objects from a baraita: one resumes from the beginning of the blessing in which he erred.
moves.about: the baraita says one returns to the beginning of the blessing in which he erred, against Rav Huna's ruling that one returns to the beginning of the section

moves.summary: The baraita is declared a refutation of Rav Huna.
moves.about: the baraita's 'from the beginning of the blessing in which he erred' is declared a refutation of Rav Huna

moves.summary: On Rav Huna's behalf: the middle blessings are all one blessing, so 'beginning of the blessing' means the start of the middle section.
moves.about: the middle blessings are all one blessing, so 'the beginning of the blessing' means the beginning of the middle section

moves.summary: Rav Yehuda: one asks his own needs only in the middle blessings, not in the first or last three.
moves.about: R' Chanina's parable of the servant praising, requesting and taking leave, adduced as the reason for Rav Yehuda's rule

moves.summary: R' Chanina's parable — servant praising, requesting, taking leave — is adduced as the reason.
moves.about: R' Chanina's parable grounds Rav Yehuda's rule that personal requests belong only in the middle blessings

moves.summary: Baraita: a student led prayer before R' Eliezer and prolonged excessively.
moves.about: two incidents of students leading prayer before R' Eliezer, one too long and one too short

moves.summary: The students complain: how long-winded he is.
moves.about: the students complain that the prayer leader is long-winded

moves.summary: R' Eliezer: is he longer than Moses, who prayed forty days and nights?
moves.about: the student is no longer than Moses, who prayed forty days and nights

moves.summary: Parallel incident: a student led prayer before R' Eliezer and abbreviated excessively.
moves.about: a student led prayer before R' Eliezer and abbreviated excessively

moves.summary: The students complain: how brief he is.
moves.about: the students complain that the prayer leader is too brief

moves.summary: R' Eliezer: is he briefer than Moses, who prayed 'please, God, heal her, please'?
moves.about: the student is no briefer than Moses, whose prayer for Miriam was five words
